title: Five Players to Watch at OTAs | Baltimore Ravens Final Drive
text: Happy Monday, Ravens flock. The Ravens started organized team activities, OTAAS, today as the next phase of the offseason program begins. This phase contains voluntary onfield practices, which the team can hold 10 of before mandatory camp in June. It's the first time the rookies will be participating with the vets and organized team activities and all eyes will be on first round pick Manga Awan as he works to build rapport with the Ravens starting offensive line and nail down timing with the Ravens offense throughout the offseason program. It will also be important for rookie receivers Jacobe Lane and Elijah Serat to get a feel for operating in a Lamar Jackson run offense and Jackson will learn his new weapons tendencies and strengths as the summer progresses. Perhaps not as glamorous of a pick, but punter Ryan Eckley will be expected to come in and be effective right away, replacing Pro Bowler Jordan Stout, who departed in free agency. And in tonight's episode of Wired, senior special teams coach Randy Brown refers to Ekley as a young Sam Cook, the Ravens highly respected punter of 16 years. So, big shoes to fill. And coming into his sophomore season, I'm excited to see what safety Malachi Starks brings into year two. Starks played in all 17 games as a rookie and is a player I expect to see take a big jump with a full season's experience under his belt. And finally, who isn't excited to see Trey Hendrickson on the field in a Ravens uniform? We got to see him during veteran mini camp earlier this off season, but it's still feels surreal. Hendrickson has been a fixture in the building throughout the offseason program, and after ending his last season with Cincinnati Uninjured Reserve, it's clear Hendrickson is itching to get back to real action. Something I'm sure head coach and defensive play caller Jesse Mentor is also looking forward to. The Ravens will hold media availability tomorrow, which will be available to stream on our YouTube channel, app, and website. Thanks for watching. We'll be back with you tomorrow.

But again, these guys flying around, building those foundations, playing within each other, whatever 11 guys are out there, to me that's a successful camp. Every team I've ever been a part of has left and said we just had a successful camp. Then you got to go you got to go do it with the pads on, you got to continue to get better. So like how that gets judged, I don't know. I mean we we just been around it for a long time and I know I'm getting long-winded with it. I'd say the second part of it is though is getting these guys out healthy. So how can we compete as hard as we flat out can, but also, you know, within the the rules in terms of not being in pads and all that and keeping these guys healthy ready to go come late July. Mac had said something on Saturday he was excited to go against your offense and he had to of a competitive ness to it. Do you have that as well, where you want to get out here and kind of just go against Nick's defense? >> Yeah, absolutely. I mean, it's you know, I've I've gone against a few of these players, quote-unquote, you know, for for a few years, and obviously just being in this division, but you know, I I love those guys on on that side of the ball, but at the same time, when we're going, we're going, right? And you know, those those defensive players want to beat up on the offense, even if it's just OTA one, and and it's going to be, you know, hopefully the same for for how our guys feel going against their guys. So, yeah, it was it was fun to get out there and chop it up with them. You know, the guys that, you know, you're going to be you're going to be talking to a little bit more just by by who they are personality-wise. What kind of feedback have you gotten from the offensive guys who have been here before? The Ryans, Marvin Harrison, Arthur. Do you feel like they're connecting with with the things you're saying and implementing? Yeah, I think it again, I think it kind of goes back to they they have history of of kind of what we've done, too, right? Because they've played us twice a year, you know, some of those guys for four years, three years, what what what have you. So, I mean, they they've seen it firsthand as well. So, again, just yeah, I know it's been it's been good getting to go with them. What's the process of installing the the playbook at this point? How much is it all in, and you guys are just working on it? Like, what's the what's the process? Yeah, I mean, it started back when they first got here for phase one, right? And we spent those four days, like we discussed, where we didn't talk about one play. We were just talking about the the the pre-snap operation, the cadences, the formations, the motions, how it's all tied together. Along with that, you're talking about a lot of the fundamentals of what you're trying to get done. Don't worry about the play, here's how we hit blocks, here's how we hit interior blocks with our dual game, here's how the wide zone looks. Here's how our slides, here's our terminology. So, you spend a lot of time just doing that, and then you try to bucket it up for the guys, you know, just from a pass game standpoint, talk about all your backside progression, stuff that's coming in the quarterback's vision, why those words are what they are. Then you go to the quick game, then you bucket up into the different varieties of five-step and seven-step and all that, how all the seven-step ties in with the play-pass, and then can we sprinkle in a screen here and there, you know? And so, um with the rules, you know, you don't like you get too far ahead of yourself, well, you didn't even get a chance to go practice that stuff, you know? So, we have to be careful with I don't care about installing a screen in early April if we can't go rep it, you know, until mid-May. So, um but for the most part, I mean, yeah, I'd say we're we're we're in. How do you see the rookies kind of mesh in with the vets today? Uh good. It was obviously great to have them there for that just obviously all last week, and then even those two days of rookie, you know, we'll call it mini-camp, but uh it's really, like I said, rookie field work, particularly with the numbers that we had. So, um thought they they meshed in well. I thought uh you know, both sides looked like they could again break the huddle and just operate and and go play a little bit of ball. Um part of the question I just had, I mean, it's, you know, we're not overly trying to design stuff right now. You just want these guys to just, you know, not have to think and go play fast and get a little bit better every day. Talk about chopping it up, but some of the guys on the defensive side of the ball, Nick Cross is a very vocal guy, right? What what are you Are you guy who's going to give that back to Nick, or are you kind of like a cool-tempered guy during practice? Like, what are you in terms of like trash talk? Uh I don't I don't predetermine any of that, you know? I mean, you're just out there with the guys, and uh it you know, it's it's fun. You I mean, I who knows? We'll see where it all ends up going, but I like like messing with the dudes, ones I can handle it at least. How [snorts] how are things uh progressing with Jacoby's just contract discussions? Same as where we were a few weeks ago, so. And does that impact I guess what is the impact of not having, you know, one of your top quarterback options here during OTAs? You know, it it's uh it's not mandatory, right? And uh and like I've said with with Jacoby and all veterans I've ever been around, uh they've played football. The hardest thing to do in this league is get used to the speed of the game. And even for not just the rookie, but the second-year, third-year guy and and he's played a lot of football. Um, he's done probably everything that we've ever done schematically. It's just a little bit different verbage, you know, so um, if it's the flip stuff that that's uh, you know, getting used to the game. Like if a rookie's not here or second-year guy's not here, you're like, "Oh, crap." You know, cuz it takes a minute, so. Have you had any contact with him to install in the playbook, uh, you know, remotely with him? We've had contact. I'll I'll keep it at that. Your early impressions of Carson, what have you thought about his progression so far since getting in the building? Yeah, no, it's it was good. Like I was I was impressed with him today in terms of just um, hearing the play calls from me. That's, you know, obviously he's heard me speak. We've talked. He knows what the reads are and all that, but it's the first time he's ever heard that, you know, uh, the mic going into his helmet. So, you never know how that's going to be. I might sound muffled. I might sound like I don't know what I'm like, whatever, you know, and I thought he did a really good job of of hearing me, communicating that kind of stuff. Um, I thought, you know, Hackett and Shob did a great job of just getting all these quarterbacks just ready to go, you know, for practice again. I mean, it's sometimes OTAs and training camp are actually harder than in season in terms of just the plays because per again, going back to the point, like everything is kind of up. Now, what I tell the guys all the time, we'll never go out on the field and just throw out stuff blind on you. Uh, I I'm a big believer in recovering stuff cuz again, you know, these guys aren't sitting there as coaches and and just thinking of a million different things all day. I mean, they got they got lives outside of this thing. So, just giving them that that practice preparation in terms of what we're going to do, and then um, you know, for them to go out there and execute. I know it's early, uh, and he's on the defensive side of the ball, but what are your impressions of Will Johnson and the kind of player he can be? I was really impressed with Will as a rookie. Uh, obviously I didn't study him coming out. I did hear of him just being, you know, in that kind of first-round, second-round discussion, uh, just through throughout the Rams building. And there was there was love for him there. But then having a play him, you know, whatever it was week 10 or 11 when we when we came out here, he he is a good player, you know, and you saw um what obviously money and and and Arizona saw. Um you know, sometimes I look at some of those corners and it's like it doesn't matter really how I feel. I want to know how Stafford feels and I know how Stafford felt about him in terms of just a good young player and uh hard to like describe how you can just but you can just you can tell that he just understands ball. Like he understands the game. Um he knows what's going on out there and sometimes particularly for a veteran quarterback, that's the stuff that's tricky cuz you don't know when he's going to kind of change up and throw a little curveball out out there for you. So really impressed with him. Love the dude. Um I think he's got, you know, a high ceiling. When you when you first got here, did you go through and watch film on every guy especially on the offensive side of the ball to see kind of a whole season's worth of plays or what was your approach to that? Yeah, I mean it's yes to particularly on offense, you know, there was a little bit of a catch-up with defense and and you know, talking to Nick, talking to money and stuff like that. But again for for the guys that were out there playing like I mean that's part of my job preparing for them, right? Now unfortunately a lot of these guys weren't playing when we played them cuz a lot of them were injured, you know. So it's it's good that they're you know, going to be back because I know this there was a few guys that were out there that weren't playing in other games and those were the games that you had to study cuz it sometimes looked like two different teams out there with the amount of amount of bodies and humans that were getting thrown out there. So yeah, to answer your question, definitely on offense, it was it was really kind of a catch-up with kind of those the the backups if you will and and some of the late roster ads, you know, trying to really just get to know them a little bit more. Cody Simon seems like a guy you guys might rely on more this season. From watching his tape last year to now, what have you kind of seen him progress going into his second year? Well, that's that that one's just one practice out there, right? You know, and so um let me go watch that practice, you know, but uh I I saw stuff from Cody Simon in our last game where maybe he didn't have the play that he was capable of making and improving the next time he was out there. Like there there's tangible evidence of him within a game correcting himself, you know, whether it be him, his position coach, the coordinator, whatever it is, and seeing the improvement from one play to maybe 10 plays later. And it's like, "Ooh, he got it right there. He understood that he could have been a little bit better." And you saw that. And I think that's what I mean, you guys you guys get to know these guys. You can see that from Cody. Like he's he's an above the the shoulders kind of guy. Like he gets football and he loves football. And those are the guys that you you really look forward to working with cuz they're going to pour into it. You talked about it only being one practice. You talked about not being in training camp with like pads and how you got to do it in pads and stuff. Do you Do you ever have to like temper your like thoughts on players? Like, "Oh, that looks really good." Or, "He didn't look really good." Like do you have to like kind of take it with a grain of salt at this time of year? There's Yeah, for some, for sure. There's a There's definitely guys that you know, yeah, they're out there in T-shirt and shorts and a helmet, but it turns in a little bit different of a look when they get the the pads on, right? So, still probably trying to figure out who that is. I Again, I I know Trey looks good in T-shirt and short or pads, right? So, I mean, there's there's a few guys like that, but yeah, you got to temper it for sure. And just I mean, we shoot we get excited across the league about, you know, rookies and all that kind of stuff. It's like, let them get their feet wet a little bit. Let them get to training camp. Let's do some of those joint practices, preseason stuff like that, and you know, let them get their feet wet a little bit before we crown them or say, "Man, that wasn't right." What [snorts] can guys do this time of year on the field that could catch your attention and kind of and also the opposite. Like what can they do to be you could be like, "I don't like that effort from you." You know, I think I've used use consistency in here. Yeah, there's going to be mess-ups and all those kind of things and but can we go get that corrected and not see that mistake again? And if you're doing something well, can we consistently you know, see that? But I do think you can with without even the ball being snapped but just demeanor in the huddle, demeanor at the line of scrimmage, how these guys are breaking the huddle, how tight they are with their motions, how our defense lines getting their cleats in the ground, how fast our linebackers are making the calls out there. Like stuff that really doesn't take much talent. Like that's the stuff that to me sticks out a little bit more cuz again, there's you're not hitting right now, right? And there's there's protocols in place in terms of when it's 50/50 balls. Like it is what it is. All 32 teams. It's like you got to be smart in those situations. So one, people don't get hurt and two, we're not losing practices, right? So you know, those are the kind of the things that I'm really looking at right now just to see basically what guys look comfortable and what guys we need to continue to work with. >> Coach, with the schedule being released last week, I know we're months away, but is that the type of thing where you look at it and you just say, "Okay, cool. And we put it to the side." Or what's kind of the process once you actually receive that schedule? Outside of my wife's phone ringing about, you know, who wants to come to the home games and away games, I I don't really care about any of that. No. >> Coach, we'll make this the last one. No tip Remind today. Do you expect him to be back for the start of training camp or do you kind of have an idea of what his timeline is? Yeah, no. You know, not going to dive too far into that but do expect him to to be healthy, ready to roll when we get going, you know, in in training camp and another guy that's I had a lot of respect for coming out of Illinois and then it's like some of those guys when you when you get the job, you're like, "Yes, I wanted him coming out of the draft." And then you get to inherit him, you know, and as I can say that easily about Tip because Tip is all of the right stuff in terms of how he approaches it and stuff like that. It's unfortunate obviously what happened a year ago but uh you know, big piece of what where I think we can go. How much of that's mental? Time what? Kind of that same type of thing. Yep. Thanks guys.

title: CB Will Johnson OTA Press Conference  | Arizona Cardinals 2026
text: What's up? What's up? How you guys doing? Good. You still reveling in the dunk from the other night, other day? Nah, it was that was pretty light. Nothing too crazy. >> [snorts] >> What's it mean to wear uh number two again? Means a lot, man. It just feels feels feels right. I feel real comfortable in it, so I'm glad I was able to get that back. Was that something you had to kind of negotiate a little bit with Mack? Not really. I mean, once Kyler left, Mack was had the one on his mind and I had the two on my mind. We just coached LaFleur. He let us do it, so yeah. You were You were obviously a rookie this time of year last year. Just how much further along obviously you have a full season under your belt. How much further along do you feel now? Yeah, it's a whole different feeling going into it this year versus last year. Last year coming in with all the draft stuff and combine and I was injured coming in, so that versus, you know, having some experience and feeling comfortable in the defense is a whole different whole different feeling. It feels It feels really good this year. How much does it help you personally and [snorts] maybe as a group? I mean, obviously coach LaFleur is in there, so there's a lot of different things, but with [clears throat] Nick staying here, there's a lot of the same stuff for defensively. How much does that help you guys having some stability in that regard? Yeah, I think it helps us. I mean, like you said, we all have played in the defense, so we're still steadily growing together in the defense and I think uh we're all building chemistry and um I mean, we feel it on the field. We obviously got a lot of work to do to continue to get better, but we feel that chemistry and uh I mean, we love the defense. So, we just got to keep getting better every day. Outside of the injured guys that are coming back, you know, Star and Shawn, it's the group that you guys had last year. What's it mean to be able to kind of run it back and get to kind of uh get another crack at it defensively in the defensive secondary? Uh means a lot. I mean, uh like you said, Star, SMB. I don't know if SMB's playing nickel a little more nickel now and I mean, we got a great room. We think we got a lot of talent in that room from top to bottom, so we're going to keep pushing each other every day and try to be the best best position group in the league. What do you think having an off-season where you could just rest, and relax, not have to go through all the pre-draft process, can that help you kind of at this point going forward? Yeah, I think it's helped me a lot. Um I mean, my body feels great right now. Um you know, Kyle he's done a great job, our strength coach, you know, getting us in a good position to be ready for the season, so I think the guys feel really good out there, feel strong, feel fast, and um yeah, we're in a great spot right now. You're a DB at this time of year. Yeah, you guys can put on helmets, yeah, you can do 11 on 11. The rules are such that you're supposed to basically let the receivers have at it if at all possible. How how hard is that as a DB when you're trying to compete, but you know you're not supposed to really get too involved? I mean, when you're on the field, none of that really matters. I mean, we're out there still competing, and um you know, coach LaFleur told me last week that first play they were going to come at me, and then I got a PBU the first play today, so that that felt good to be able to talk a little smack to him after that, but yeah, we're just out there competing, and we're not really worried about that, so yeah, it's all good. Early thoughts on Carson Beck watching him today in 11 on 11? Uh he looks smooth. I mean, obviously he's a rookie, so he's probably got some things to learn on the offense, but I mean, I don't really know much about uh you know, what he's supposed to be doing out there, but I mean, from what I see, he looks pretty good out there. You talked about the continuity, and obviously that's important, but every year you want to take those steps. So, what ways might this defense, you know, it's still early, but what ways might it be a little bit different than last year? Um I think it'll just be, you know, going to play free, play hard. Um our focus is just playing hard, having a lot of effort, and um having a good culture more than we're being worried about the scheme. I think that's what we're focused on. Well, when you think about your rookie season, how do you kind of review yourself? Um I think it was solid. Um I'll give it a B- minus, C plus, something like that. I feel like I got my feet wet. Um have some good plays, had some bad plays. Got to experience a lot of good receivers. So, I think it gave me a lot of confidence I'm going into this year and more comfortability in this defense and um you know, coming in with the whatever my role will be this year. I'm excited about it and just looking to get better every day. I'll see you on that grade. It's going to be an A, right? What do you want to give yourself? But is there any part that you allow yourself some grace because it was your first NFL season and you're coming off a long off season. You're dealing with injuries. Like how do you approach kind of how you view what you did last year? Yeah, I mean I got really high expectations of myself. So, you know, anytime you know, someone catch the ball on me or anything like that, I'm pretty hard on myself. So, um my goal is to get no passes caught on me and things like that, but like you said, I mean it was a I was a rookie last year. So, there was things I hadn't experienced before. Dudes I never really went against before and things like that. So, not that and I was going through a lot of things throughout the year. So, I'm just trying to make sure I can be on the field as much as possible and I think I'll be in a good spot if I can do that. What are the kind of main things in your skill development that you're focused on kind of adding to your game or improving this off season? Really everything. I mean focusing on my body a lot, um getting that right. Um you know, footwork, ball skills, uh the mental part of the game, really really everything. Just trying to get better in all all facets of the game. Well, thank you. >> Thanks, Will. I appreciate it.
